title: Best VPS for OpenClaw: requirements and which KVM plan to pick
seoTitle: Best VPS for OpenClaw: which Hostinger KVM plan to pick
description: OpenClaw does not publish a general minimum RAM. See what each scenario asks for and which Hostinger KVM plan fits.

contentSections.heading: Quick answer
paragraphs: If the AI model runs at a provider, through an API key or Hostinger's AI credits, KVM 1, with 4 GB, is the starting point. For a local model, the documentation sets an 8 GiB floor, and KVM 4, with 16 GB, is the first plan with room to spare. If you do not want to look after a server, see the managed option below.

contentSections.heading: What the official documentation says (and does not say) about requirements
paragraphs: Where the AI model runs decides the RAM: at a provider, through your API key or Hostinger's AI credits, or locally, on the server itself. An API key is the password OpenClaw uses to request answers from a provider, which charges for usage. With the model at the provider, the request goes to the AI company and the server only runs the program.
The official installation and local-model pages say the following:
bullets: **Node version.** OpenClaw requires Node 24.16 or newer, or Node 26.1 or newer. Node is the program that runs OpenClaw, and installing through npm requires that version. The page recommends Node 26. If Node is not installed, the official installer includes the version (Node 26 on macOS and Node 24 LTS on Linux).

**Local model.** For the smallest recipe the documentation itself offers, the floor is 8 GiB of host memory, with a 64K context. The page says these floors "do not guarantee the model fits or runs at speed".

**Hostinger VPS.** Hostinger installs OpenClaw on the VPS with Docker, a program that runs each application isolated in a container. A VPS is a rented virtual server; with root access, you have full control of it.
postParagraphs: It gives no RAM, processor (vCPU) or disk figure for OpenClaw without a local model, nor a server minimum for the API key or credits scenario.

One detail on the math: 8 GiB is about 8.6 GB. KVM 2 is advertised with 8 GB, which is about 7.5 GiB, a little under the floor, and that is before counting the memory the system and Docker use. The documentation does not say whether this unit difference counts toward the floor.

contentSections.heading: How much RAM each scenario needs
paragraphs: The documentation gives a RAM figure only for the local model: RAM is the working memory, where the program and the model sit while they run.

postParagraphs: Two details on the local model. Context is the amount of text (tokens, pieces of words) the model reads at once. When less than 20% of the context window is left, OpenClaw warns, with a floor of 8 thousand tokens; below 10%, it blocks the answer, with a floor of 4 thousand tokens.
None of the KVM plan pages checked lists a graphics card (GPU). The documentation also does not say how fast a local model would run without one.

bullets: **KVM 1 (4 GB).** Starting point for the API key or credits scenario. For a local model, it is below the official floor.
**KVM 2 (8 GB).** For an API key, there is room to spare. For a local model, it sits at the floor, with no margin for the system.
**KVM 4 (16 GB).** The first plan with room above the official 8 GiB floor. The documentation does not say how well it performs with a local model.
**KVM 8 (32 GB).** Makes sense only with a larger local model. The documentation does not say how much memory each large recipe needs.

contentSections.heading: VPS, running at home or managed: which scenario needs what
paragraphs: The three paths run the same program, OpenClaw, with different costs and workloads. The choice depends on three things: whether you want to work on a server, whether your computer can stay on 24 hours, and whether the AI model is in the cloud or runs on your own hardware.

contentSections.heading: The free VPS: Oracle Always Free
paragraphs: You can test for free on Oracle: Always Free is not Hostinger's, does not replace the paid VPS, and an idle instance can be reclaimed. According to Oracle's documentation:
bullets: Up to two Micro instances (AMD processor), with 1/8 OCPU and 1 GB of memory each.
Arm Ampere A1 instances: 2 OCPUs and 12 GB of memory in total, which you split as you like. The monthly limit is 1,500 OCPU hours and 9,000 GB-hours.
200 GB of block storage in total, for the system and extra disks, with up to five backups.
Free instances must be created in the account's home region. Creating one elsewhere is billed.
postParagraphs: The rule that matters: Oracle says it may reclaim an idle instance. An instance counts as idle when, over a 7-day period, CPU use at the 95th percentile stays below 20%, network use stays below 20% and, on A1, memory use also stays below 20%. An assistant that sits idle most of the time can fall under this rule. The documentation describes no advance notice before reclaiming.

contentSections.heading: Which to choose, in short
paragraphs: The plan choice follows where the AI model runs and how much server work you want to take on.
bullets: Model in the cloud, through the API key or Hostinger's AI credits: KVM 1, with 4 GB, as the starting point.
Local model: KVM 4, with 16 GB, the first plan with room above the official 8 GiB floor. KVM 8, with 32 GB, makes sense only with a larger local model.
If you do not want to look after a server: the managed option, where Hostinger installs and updates the assistant.
To test without paying: Oracle Always Free, knowing that Oracle can reclaim an idle instance.

contentSections.heading: Frequently asked questions
bullets: What is the minimum server for OpenClaw? The official documentation publishes no minimum RAM, CPU or disk; it requires Node 24.16 or newer (or 26.1). With an API key or credits, KVM 1 is the starting point. With a local model, the floor is 8 GiB, and KVM 4 is the first with room to spare.

Can you run it without an API key? Yes, with a local model, but then memory becomes the problem: the documentation gives 8 GiB as the floor for its smallest local recipe, with a 64K context, and warns that this does not guarantee the model fits or runs well. With Hostinger's credits, you do not need an account with an AI provider, but you pay for usage.

Is Oracle really free? Yes, as long as the account stays within Always Free: 2 OCPUs and 12 GB on the Arm A1, plus the Micro instances. An instance that sits idle for 7 days, with CPU, network and memory below 20%, can be reclaimed by Oracle.
Mac mini or VPS? It depends on whether the computer can stay on 24 hours. If it can, running at home removes the server fee; if it cannot, choose a VPS or the managed option.

Is there a Hostinger discount coupon for an OpenClaw VPS? Yes: the code SONAR20, in the cart's coupon field, gives 20% off the first period. The 20% also apply on renewal; check the price in the cart.
